case: Eurodrone fictional eco-design and supply resilience

cues.text: In ASRI, we will examine supply chain resilience and eco-design using the Eurodrone case.
We select Create Your Own Strategic Case to evaluate decisions from an operational perspective.
In Investigate, we choose Eurodrone and focus on decisions involving critical materials.
Select Eco-design and Critical Materials. ASRI loads the case definition and three comparable alternatives.
The case definition identifies a support subsystem and the scope of the decision under review.
The question is whether repair and supplier diversification can reduce in-service vulnerabilities.
Before comparing, we set the same component, functional requirement and assessment period.
We continue to Challenge, where operating and economic conditions drive the results.
We compare the current baseline, qualified repair and a combined option with an alternative supplier.
All six sections follow the same structure. Only the applicable parameters differ.
Open Operational Conditions. Each input shows the three options using equivalent units.
Recovery time indicates how long each option takes without additional incidents.
The binding supply lead time reflects the wait for a component or supplier when it affects the decision.
The deadline is shared. ASRI evaluates whether each strategy could meet it given the stated risks.
Open Risks and Probabilities to enter success likelihood and potential disruptions.
We distinguish technical success probability from the delay caused by failure of the chosen route.
We also assess the possibility of an external disruption and the additional days it could cause.
Economic Obligations covers direct costs, logistics and additional commitments under disruption.
Expected cost weights those expenses by probability to compare options within the same boundary.
Contractual Conditions lets us assess reservations and penalties whenever those obligations apply.
If a condition is irrelevant, mark it Not Applicable and record why, rather than inventing a zero.
Environmental Factors covers materials, waste and greenhouse gases within a defined boundary.
These indicators reveal trade-offs between circularity, availability and cost.
The sixth section covers evidence and uncertainty: every input needs an appropriate source and review.
The dashboard compares time, deadline attainment, cost and environmental outcomes without imposing a winner.
We change the recovery time for the repair option to test how the model responds.
The calculation updates immediately, allowing us to examine sensitivity before deciding.
We restore the original value to keep the comparison consistent.
The sensitivity margin shows whether conclusions depend strongly on a particular assumption.
One option may improve one indicator and worsen another. ASRI makes those trade-offs visible.
We move to Check to identify which conclusions are adequately supported.
Check shows how the Eurodrone exercise is documented, from assumptions through review and traceability.
All four methodological gates are checked within this complete simulated exercise.
These are exercise-only reviews. ASRI makes that distinction clear without leaving our demonstration unfinished.
The register contains eighteen fictional records, with accountable teams, reviewers, dates and limitations.
Each record is organised by option and topic, covering operations, technical risks, supply, cost and environment.
All seventeen applicable inputs in every option are linked to exercise records marked as reviewed.
Both alternative comparisons show the exercise as complete, with no missing evidence or methodology gates.
Now we arrive at Translate, where ASRI turns a completed analysis into meaningful strategic decisions.
Translate is the core of ASRI. It explains the operational value behind sustainability choices.
It asks what vulnerability changes, not merely which environmental indicator improves.
We can connect repairability to recovery options, supplier dependence and continuity of support.
The underlying figures stay the same while the decision-focused interpretation changes.
The analysis distinguishes a completed exercise from formally approved operational evidence.
First, consider the Defence Customer. Their concern is restoring the required capability.
The headline now explains why having another recovery route matters when supply is disrupted.
The decision is whether the option meets operational requirements and restores the component sooner.
Here, estimated component recovery falls from one hundred forty one point three to ninety two days.
The benefit concerns component recovery in this scenario, not a guaranteed increase in fleet availability.
Below the headline, seven deeper conclusions explain the strategic significance of the results.
First, the binding constraint. Repair work takes sixty five days, but supply still takes seventy eight.
Shortening repair alone cannot remove that seventy eight day supply constraint. We must address the bottleneck.
Next, ASRI shows assumed disruption likelihood, technical success and the modelled chance of meeting the deadline.
The cost analysis reveals whether faster recovery comes with savings, or requires an additional premium.
Environmental trade-offs are also explicit: material, waste and bounded emissions can move in different directions.
Crucially, ASRI compares the selected strategy with the other proposed option, not just the baseline.
It then evaluates review coverage and sensitivity, without disguising assumptions as observed outcomes.
Finally, each audience gets a concrete next decision, with appropriate conditions for validation.
Now choose Engineering. The same scenario becomes a technical qualification decision.
Engineering focuses on repair viability, safety, traceability and functional equivalence.
Which tests and authorisations would allow this recovery route to be used safely?
The action section turns that question into a practical set of engineering checks.
Switch to Programme Management. Here, timing, expected cost and commitments take centre stage.
The recovery result connects directly to milestone risk and the time available to respond.
The model compares how much faster the option recovers and how likely it is to meet its deadline.
The economic analysis also shows whether that resilience comes with savings or a premium.
Finally, choose Executive Leadership and view the broader industrial resilience argument.
The same evidence now supports decisions on repair capability and supply-chain dependence.
Leadership can see which constraints are binding, and where investment may change the outcome.
Instead of generic claims, ASRI suggests a bounded next decision and what would justify it.
Leadership can revisit the risk assumptions and see which dependencies remain exposed.
The evidence section keeps the distinction between simulated reviews and actual programme authorisation.
One consistent analytical model now supports four audiences, with no change to the underlying facts.
Switch from qualified repair to repair plus alternative sourcing. The interpretation changes immediately.
This combined option introduces a second sourcing route alongside repair, and changes the comparative result.
Its additional resilience must still be weighed against cost. ASRI makes that compromise visible.
ASRI shows the scenario boundary clearly. A complete tutorial does not imply programme approval.
These seven conclusions will also be generated for any future case built with the same tool.
The real value is translating sustainability into resilience, risk, trade-offs and actionable choices.
These expanded conclusions can also be exported with the full comparison and traceable exercise records.
The PDF report brings together the case, results, evidence and audience-specific interpretation.
A Markdown version is also available for reviewing and editing the content.
Before any external use, replace simulated records with verified sources and obtain the required approvals.
We can download an editable case file and continue the analysis whenever needed.
ASRI gives customers and teams a richer strategic conversation, grounded in alternatives, evidence and resilience.

storyline: English tutorial re-recorded against live current ASRI, complete Check and seven strategic insights, no missing exercise evidence.
